_readme: config.json for tinycmdr. One example, every key, fake values.
The installer copies this file to config.json and fills in the values below from
its own flags, or from the answers you give it. If you are writing one by hand,
copy this and replace the placeholder values. Delete any key you do not care
about and the code's default applies; the values shown ARE those defaults
except where a _comment says otherwise.
What each lane needs before it starts (nothing else is mandatory):
a Mattermost bot     mattermost.url, mattermost.allowed_users, and a bot token.
The token belongs in .env as TINYCMDR_MM_TOKEN: leave the
copy here empty, because this is a file the agent can read
into a prompt.
a Telegram DM        TINYCMDR_TG_TOKEN in .env, and telegram.allowed_users with
your NUMERIC id (message @userinfobot for it). Mattermost
wins when both tokens are set, so a Telegram-only process
is:  python tinycmdr.py --telegram
a session by hand    nothing:   python tinycmdr.py --cli
llm.base_url and llm.model are NOT checked at start: a wrong endpoint shows up as a
run that fails, and `tinycmdr doctor` names it. mattermost.* is unused by the
Telegram lane, and telegram.* by the Mattermost lane.
Addresses here are deliberately unroutable documentation ranges
(192.0.2.0/24, example.com), so copying this file cannot accidentally point
at somebody's real service. A token does NOT belong in this file.

llm._comment: Which endpoint answers, and how hard it is allowed to work. base_url is any OpenAI-compatible /v1 root; a local llama.cpp, vLLM or Ollama box, or a cloud provider. Sampling (temperature, top_p, top_k) is deliberately NOT configurable: it is inherited from whatever endpoint you point at, so switching models or providers cannot leave a stale setting behind.
llm._comment_context: max_context_tokens is a CEILING on the messages payload, not a promise: the harness asks the endpoint what it serves per request (a llama.cpp box answers /v1/models or /props), keeps room for the reply and the tool schemas, and uses the tighter of the two. "auto" (or 0, or blank) means believe the endpoint, and is what ships - a number written for one box becomes the wrong number the moment that box is restarted with a different slot count, and the run then dies mid-think with no answer. If your endpoint reports nothing about its window (most hosted APIs), auto falls back to a conservative 8000 and the log says so: put the number your provider documents here instead.
llm._comment_context_window: context_window says what the model's window IS: 'auto' (or 0/blank) asks the endpoint - llama.cpp answers /v1/models or /props, vLLM max_model_len, Ollama /api/ps, SGLang /get_server_info - and a NUMBER pins it when a local server will not answer. A busy llama.cpp box can time out one probe; the harness retries a miss in 20s instead of caching the empty answer for the full five-minute TTL. A pinned window wins over detection, and max_context_tokens still caps the messages payload on top of it.
llm._comment_window_presets: Host-substring -> tokens for endpoints that report NO window (most hosted APIs), consulted before the built-in table (api.openai.com 128k, api.anthropic.com 200k, api.deepseek.com 128k - their own docs, checked 2026-10-04). max_context_tokens still caps whatever this says. Put your provider's documented number here when its window differs from the built-in - e.g. {"api.deepseek.com": 1000000} - and doctor/setup name this lever for an off-LAN endpoint on an assumed window.
llm._max_call_seconds: No single generation gets more than this many SECONDS at the decode rate the endpoint last measured (from its own usage line). 16,384 tokens is a six-minute generation at 45 tok/s and half an hour at 8 - both measured on macOS while requests shared the endpoint's two slots. 0 disables it, and an endpoint that has not reported a rate yet leaves the cap alone.
llm._comment_same_endpoint_retry: 408/5xx and transport failures (refused/reset connections, socket timeouts) retry the SAME endpoint with capped exponential backoff plus jitter before any endpoint failover, because a local box answers 503 while it loads a model and demoting that to another model silently changes what the conversation runs on. Backoff is min(retry_base_ms x 2^(n-1), retry_max_ms) x (75-100%); a provider Retry-After/X-RateLimit-Reset hint that is longer wins. 0 disables the same-endpoint retry and restores immediate failover.
llm._comment_replay_reasoning: Assistant reasoning_content is replayed on history turns to LOCAL endpoints: a llama.cpp/vLLM chat template rebuilds the <think> block from it, which keeps the replayed prefix byte-aligned turn to turn (a diverging prefix throws away the KV-cache hit from that point, on every turn, for the models that emit the most tokens). A remote endpoint never receives the field. replay_reasoning_max_chars bounds what a long think block re-buys each turn.
llm._comment_prompt_cache_key: Sticky-routing hint for remote endpoints: OpenAI and Moonshot take `prompt_cache_key`, and OpenRouter routes stickily on the same field (its docs call it `session_id`). `auto` derives one value per conversation from the session key, fixed across a compaction, which is the APIs' own guidance; `off` sends none; any other string is sent as-is (256 chars max). A host that answers 400 naming the field is remembered and never asked again. Local endpoints never get it.
llm._comment_reasoning_flags: Paired preservation flags for a host whose docs say the echoed reasoning is INERT without them (Z.AI: {"clear_thinking": false}; Fireworks: {"reasoning_history": "preserved"}). Merged into the request only when the endpoint itself has been learned to take the echo back, which is what keeps this a config lever instead of a vendor table.

fallbacks._comment: Optional. Tried in order when the primary fails. alias is what /model <alias> switches to. Prefer api_key_env over api_key so the secret stays in .env.

llm._stream: Model calls use SSE when true: the first token is visible while it generates, a cancel closes the socket (a local llama.cpp stops generating), and a wedged stream ends on stream_idle_seconds. false = one blocking POST per call, which is what every version before 1.9.28 did.
llm._llama_extensions: true (default) asks a llama.cpp endpoint for its OWN stream extensions: return_progress (a prompt_progress event at ~0.1s and then once per prompt batch, rendered as "reading prompt · N%" - a long prompt is otherwise minutes of silence) and, when sse_ping_interval is set, the keep-alive SSE comment. Gated on that endpoint's own /props reply confirming a llama.cpp build, and only ever asked of an on-LAN endpoint: a cloud provider rejects an unknown request field with a 400 and no other local server promises to ignore one. false = never send them. Neither field changes the model's answer.
llm._sse_ping_interval: 0 = the server's own default (30s on llama.cpp), N = a ping every N seconds, -1 = no pings. Only ever sent to a confirmed llama.cpp endpoint.
llm._window_profiles: Caps for a WINDOW BAND, keyed by the window the endpoint actually serves. `profiles` above follows the model's NAME, which cannot help the common self-hosted case: the same box restarted with a different quantisation or slot count, or a model whose name says nothing about its window. The SMALLEST band at least as large as the served window wins (a box serving 12288 takes the 16384 entry). Only keys the harness already reads are accepted, and a band's values are undone when a later band takes over, so only the last band applied is in force. The three below are the documented starting point for a small self-hosted model - delete them to get the window-scaled defaults, which already shrink every character cap to window/8. The character caps are ceilings: on an 8k window they clamp at 1024, which is the point. A band CAPS the character budgets only - it never widens the window, so it cannot fix a cloud endpoint the harness is running on its assumed 8000 (which lands in the 16384 band and gets small-model caps). Only llm.max_context_tokens sets the window; put the provider's documented number there.
llm._comment_reasoning: reasoning: auto sends no reasoning field at all, which is the honest default - a server keeps its own. A level (minimal, low, medium, high, xhigh, max) asks for it in whatever shape the endpoint takes: reasoning_effort for an OpenAI-compatible /chat/completions, reasoning.effort for /responses, thinking.budget_tokens for an Anthropic-style endpoint (see llm.reasoning_mode to force a shape, llm.reasoning_wire to remap a level's spelling, llm.thinking_budgets to override the token table).

telegram._comment: The third door: a Telegram DM. OFF unless you set TINYCMDR_TG_TOKEN in .env - the token is ENV-ONLY, so one pasted at 'token' below is ignored (and logged as ignored), because .env is the one place the agent cannot read into a prompt. allowed_users takes NUMERIC Telegram ids (message @userinfobot for yours) and is deny-by-default: an empty list starts the process, refuses, and says the id is missing. Mattermost WINS when both doors have a token, so this lane never starts on a Mattermost bot - run `python tinycmdr.py --telegram` for a Telegram-only process. DM only: a group message is refused. It shares the same sessions, notes, tasks and skills as every other door.

mattermost._comment: Where the bot lives. url is the host only, scheme and port are separate keys. token: leave empty and set TINYCMDR_MM_TOKEN in .env instead - .env is the one place the agent cannot read into a prompt. allowed_users are Mattermost USER IDS, not usernames (Profile -> copy the id), and the list is deny-by-default. ssl_verify false is for a self-signed certificate on your own LAN.

web._comment: The page: the default door. ON by default - a bare `tinycmdr` serves it and opens a browser when the machine has one. The token is MANDATORY and lives in .env as TINYCMDR_WEB_TOKEN (the installer mints one, and so does the first start of a host that has none; `tinycmdr token set TINYCMDR_WEB_TOKEN` with an empty value mints a fresh one and prints the link). No token = no server, never an open port. host 127.0.0.1 keeps it on this machine; a headless box reached from the LAN sets host to 0.0.0.0 (the installer and `tinycmdr setup` ask), where the token travels in cleartext - use it on a network you trust. 8790 is the published default (8787 belongs to RStudio Server). a2a true adds the A2A v1.0 endpoint (/a2a plus a public agent card at /.well-known/agent-card.json; the page token as a Bearer) - off by default.

search._comment: Web search for the web_search tool. `providers` is tried in order; each entry names its own endpoint (url) and the .env variable that holds its key (api_key_env). A `searxng` entry pointing at a box on your LAN is the only shape whose traffic stays on your network. `allow_cloud_egress` is ON by default - a box with providers configured wants to search, and a silent refusal reads as a broken tool; set it false to REFUSE every off-LAN provider, which also refuses fetch_url for a URL off this network. A searxng provider never needs the flag. The installers ask (--search-egress), setup asks, and .env can carry TINYCMDR_SEARCH_EGRESS / TINYCMDR_SEARCH_PROVIDERS instead.

agent._comment: Behaviour: names, budgets, progress reporting, guard rails. The defaults are conservative for a small local model; the numbers below are what the code ships unless a _comment says otherwise.
agent._comment_budgets: Per-segment ceilings: max_steps counts tool calls and max_minutes is wall clock for ONE segment; auto_continue can open extra segments on the same task (auto_continue_max bounds them, and llm.max_turns bounds the whole run). When a cap is reached with work unfinished the harness either continues or forces a summary, so a run always ends with an answer instead of silence.
agent._comment_shell: The Windows interpreter, and a CONSOLE-BUILD setting: the cut-down build reads this and can run cmd (/c) or PowerShell, for hosts where PowerShell is restricted or removed. The supervised build ignores it and always runs PowerShell on Windows, bash -c on Linux and macOS.
agent._comment_scan_bound: The ceilings on a broad scan. A command that walks a whole root is classified as a scan: it gets search_timeout seconds instead of shell_timeout, and the seconds it actually spends are charged against one per-run budget shared by shell and execute_code. Both are on by default, because the measured failure was a run spending minutes walking a root and someone waiting; command_cost_guard false lifts the whole thing and scan_budget_seconds 0 lifts only the per-run half. Measured on the graded set: the worst command fell from 608 s to 60 s, and the run budget did not fire in a two-sample probe.
agent._comment_result_shaping: What the agent is handed after a tool runs. digestion renders a known command shape (journalctl, systemctl status, apt/dnf/pip, docker ps, grep, process lists, *.log files) down to its signal, says what it dropped, and any call may pass raw=true for the full text. field notes append the known cause to a FAILED result whose signature is understood, read from field_notes_file: keep that library small, and only for signatures that essentially always mean that cause, because a note that guesses wrong costs steps. verify_after_write parses a file the agent just wrote (python, json, toml, yaml, bash, plus the custom-tool contract) and puts the verdict in the same result; it costs no prompt tokens.
agent._comment_search_scope: search_files shows at most this many matches per file before naming the file in a capped-note (the walk is path-ordered and a capped walk says the rest was not searched). Without it one hot log can eat the whole max_results budget before the other files are reached.
agent._comment_prune_superseded: A newer read of a file blanks the older copies to a notice, so a read->edit->read loop stops paying for every version until the whole conversation is compacted. The suffix gate is the point: blanking a result inside a warm prompt-cache prefix forces the provider to re-write everything after it, so a candidate is blanked now only when the messages after it cost less than prune_suffix_tokens, or after the session has been idle for prune_idle_secs (the cache is cold by then).
agent._comment_tool_carry: Carried tool results (ON by default since 1.0.0). A session's earlier tool results can ride into the next run of the same session, bounded per result and in total, newest first, deduped by tool and arguments, age-stamped and marked when a file has changed since it was read. Measured on a live install: the later runs of a session re-bought 80% and 78% less source text, on four measured runs per leg. It ships OFF, because the failure mode that matters - answering from stale carried text - is the least tested thing here; a host that wants it sets tool_carry true. Evidence: one install runs it on deliberately so the live log keeps producing data.
agent._comment_disclosure: Tool disclosure. The request carries a small always-visible tool set (the five primitives plus the doors the standing instructions name) and the rest is revealed on demand: find_tools asks for what you want, or the agent simply calls a tool by name and the harness honours it and keeps it for the session. Re-measured 2026-10-03 (2,087 calls / 133 runs): the visible schemas are 1,702 of the 5,709 static tokens, and 79.5% of calls hit the five primitives, so this is still the biggest single saving per call. core_tools overrides the visible list; tool_disclosure false sends the whole registry again, which is the rollback. reveal_ttl_secs expires a revealed schema after that many seconds without a call (the name stays listed and a call re-reveals it); 0 disables the decay.
agent._comment_tool_index: The tool index in the static prompt. The tools this box has added are listed by CATEGORY with their NAMES on the line, and that list is capped, because a description line per tool grows with the tool count: measured 2026-09-25, one custom tool cost 167.8 chars / 49.4 tokens of the prompt on EVERY call, unbounded (80 tools took the prompt from 2,920 to 6,870 est-tok, +16 s of prefill on a LAN host). The descriptions and arguments are one find_tools call away - find_tools {category: "files & edit"} - and a tool file can declare its own shelf: CATEGORY = "..." at module level in a .py, "category" in a .tool.json manifest. Overflow renders inside these two caps as "... +N more (find_tools {category: ...})".
agent._comment_atlas: The machine atlas. The harness hands the model the facts about the box it is on - os, shell, install path, and what lives where - because a small model does not look around and then guesses paths (the most common tool error on the graded eval). It rides the TRAILING state block, on the first turn of a run and again after any failure that reads like a wrong path, never in the system prompt. atlas.md is generated on each host at first run and is never shipped in a package, so no host's map travels to another box; hand-written '## notes' in it are the curated half.
agent._comment_shell_facts: States this process's rights in the trailing block on the first turn of a run: elevated or not, and what that means for admin-only work. Measured reason: a console build launched from an ordinary terminal on an administrator account hit Access is denied and reported it as a mystery. An account being an administrator is not the same as the process being elevated (UAC gives an admin two tokens).
agent._comment_event_log: Append one JSONL line per event to sessions/<key>.events.jsonl: run start/end, tool call, tool result WITH its outcome, and reveal/eject when the wire's tool block changes, arguments scrubbed and digested rather than stored raw. SHADOW ONLY - nothing reads it back yet and no prompt or history derives from it, so turning it on changes no behaviour. Off unless you ask for it; a host that enables it can compare the events against tinycmdr.log.
agent._comment_plan: The run's plan is held by the HARNESS, not by the model: it is re-sent every turn in the trailing block with the position (calls used and left) and the step statuses. plan_from_request parses a request that lists its own steps into the plan, which is the path that actually gets used: measured, the model never chose to write a plan itself in 19 runs. plan_drift_after is how many tool calls may pass with no step moving before the harness says so; plan_max_steps bounds what a plan may carry; plan_enabled false removes all of it (the eval uses it to measure the feature on one build).
agent._comment_plan_mode: plan_requires_approval makes a session START in plan mode: the machine is read-only until the operator approves with `/plan apply` (or answers the approval question raised when the model records the plan). `/plan on` turns it on for one session, `/plan off` resumes execution.
agent._comment_context_files: AGENTS.md / CLAUDE.md found from the run's cwd up to the project (or home) root are read at session start into the static prompt: one file per directory depth (AGENTS.md wins over CLAUDE.md there), far-to-near so the nearest file is most prominent, a farther file whose paragraphs are all inside a nearer one dropped, and the block bounded by context_files_max_chars. It rides the cached prefix, so the cost is one prefill per session. These are local conventions and rank below the operator's current instruction; set context_files false to disable.
agent._comment_memory: Durable memory is an OKF bundle under memory/: one markdown concept per fact with YAML frontmatter - type (required), title, description, tags, then provenance (sources), trust (generated/verified), lifecycle (status/stale_after). index.md rides in the trailing state block, never the system prompt: the system prompt has to stay byte-stable for the endpoint's prefix cache. memory_concept_max_chars caps one concept at write time (refused, never truncated), memory_index_max_chars bounds what the prompt carries, memory_max_concepts bounds the bundle, memory_dup_overlap is the body overlap at which add refuses a restatement (update it, or say supersedes: <id> to replace). Every index line states its verification tier - unverified is the default and rides as such. notes.md is legacy - still read into the prompt, no longer written by a tool.
agent._comment_a2ui: render_ui draws A2UI v1.0 cards in the web page (createSurface envelopes against this build's catalog: Card, Column, Row, Text, Divider; data bindings resolve against createSurface.dataModel). ui_payload_max_chars bounds one card; the payload rides the transcript line and never the prompt, and a lane with no surface answers honestly instead of pretending.
agent._comment_a2a: Two halves, both off by default. Server: web.a2a true publishes an AgentCard at /.well-known/agent-card.json and answers A2A v1.0 JSON-RPC on POST /a2a (the page token as a Bearer; SendMessage runs one message and returns a Task). Client: a2a_remotes is a map of name -> {url, token_env}; the hidden `a2a` tool exists only when this map is non-empty, so a box with no peers pays no prompt bytes. a2a_timeout bounds one remote call.
agent._comment_mcp: MCP stdio servers, off until configured: mcp_servers is a map of name -> {command, args, env?}. The hidden `mcp` tool lets the model list a server's tools and call one; with an empty map no mcp tool exists at all. The client speaks the stateless 2026-07-28 revision (version and client identity in each request's _meta) and falls back once to the older initialize handshake when a server refuses it. mcp_timeout bounds one request.
agent._comment_progress: Progress must arrive as NEW messages: an edited status line notifies nobody, which is how a real 32-minute run looked like total silence. checkin_minutes and checkin_steps are the two independent cadences (either one posts), 0 turns one off.
agent._comment_stall: Stall guard. One worker serves a channel, so a wedged run would queue every later message behind it in silence. After stall_warn_minutes with no output it posts a visible 'still on it'; after stall_abandon_minutes it abandons the run and takes the next message.
agent._comment_loops: Loop guards for weak models. loop_dedupe_after refuses an identical call (same tool, same args, same output) after that many real runs and hands back the cached result; 0 disables it. loop_stop_repeats forces the final report when a call repeats that many times.
agent._comment_restate: A model that keeps RESTATING the same status is not moving either. The reporter folds the repeat into the line already on screen (no second post, no second notification) and the run says it out loud once, then wraps up with the report it already has. Any write or edit clears the count, so real work never reaches it. 0 disables either half.
agent._comment_catchup: A websocket reconnect does not replay what you missed, so the bot sweeps channels it has seen for posts from the gap. catch_up_seconds 0 turns the sweep off; catch_up_max_minutes bounds how far back it will ever reach.
agent._comment_safety: Two tiers, and neither is a security boundary. blocked_patterns is an ABSOLUTE refusal: nothing approves it in-band, and its refusal text tells the agent to ask you to run the command by hand or to take that pattern out of this list. confirm_patterns is the middle tier: a matching shell command or a matching execute_code source is ASKED about first, and a lane with nobody to ask (a scheduled job, a sub-agent) declines - see confirm_without_door. These lists are the SHIPPED ones (guard list v3); REPLACING one makes this box less protected, and `tinycmdr doctor` will say which shipped patterns are missing and exit non-zero. Add your own with blocked_patterns_extra / confirm_patterns_extra / confirm_content_patterns_extra instead - extras are appended, never substituted. Both tiers are matched case-insensitively against the command text and, for execute_code, the source text; code that assembles a command at runtime is invisible to a regex, which is exactly why an over-broad block is worse than a confirm. Recursive deletes are gated on the TARGET in code (a whole tree is refused, a named directory is confirmed) - do not try to express that here.
agent._comment_authority: Per-tool authority on top of the two regex tiers. approval_mode is a ceiling: 'auto' (the default) adds no prompts, 'write' asks before exec-tier tools (shell, execute_code, schedule, delegate_task), 'ask' asks before write and exec; 'yolo' is an alias of auto. tool_policy maps a tool name to 'deny' or 'prompt' regardless of the mode (e.g. {"shell": "deny"} makes the agent explain instead of running commands), and a tool not in the built-in tier table - any drop-in - is treated as exec, so a stricter mode fails closed. allow_patterns / allow_content_patterns are checked before the confirm tier: one known-safe command or file shape can be whitelisted instead of turning the whole tier off with confirm-allow {"all": true}. blocked_patterns still wins over everything.
agent._comment_confirm_door: confirm_without_door is what a lane with nobody to ask decides: a scheduled job or a sub-agent. decline (the default) skips the command and says so; allow runs it, which is a deliberate choice for a fleet whose jobs are trusted.
agent._comment_endpoint_tools: The endpoint gate covers TOOLS as well as shell: a custom tool whose name or description carries one of these markers stops or restarts the model endpoint this bot talks to, so it needs your confirmation - and it is REFUSED outright while the catch-up sweep says posts were lost. Name your own launchers here; nothing is hard-coded per box.
agent._comment_ask_user: ask_user lets a run STOP and ask you a question, then carry on with your answer. Off by default: with it on the model can spend budget parked on a question, so switch it on where a human watches the channel. ask_user_wait_seconds bounds that wait (5..900; the model cannot extend it, and a /stop releases a parked run immediately).
agent._comment_extras: vision: only set true if the endpoint actually accepts images - this is what lets a screenshot-returning tool (computer_use) reach the model; `tinycmdr doctor` says whether it is on and whether the endpoint agrees. subagent_model pins delegate_task sub-agents somewhere specific (empty = inherit the conversation's model). show_usage puts the token/time footer on the Done line. debug_dump_dir writes every request body to that directory when troubleshooting a model that answers nonsense (empty = off). announce_restart controls the 'back up' post after /restart.
agent._comment_jobs: A shell command still running after auto_background_seconds is handed to the process tool's table (same guards) instead of holding the turn; you are told when it finishes and can fetch the output with process {"action": "output"}. A settled job is announced once, and only if it ended within jobs_push_window_minutes, so a restart does not replay an old table. Set auto_background_seconds 0 to always block.
agent._stream_notes: When true, the model’s own narration is streamed into ONE message that grows while it writes, so the plan is readable (and stoppable or steerable) before the tools run. False restores posting it once, after the call returns.
agent._comment_mint: The model sees one run at a time, so it cannot know that the same by-hand procedure has now run four times this week. The harness keeps that census (logs/procedure-census.json) and, at mint_hint_after separate runs of one command shape, rides a single line on the tool result naming the mint call. After a run that drove mint_offer_steps or more hand calls (shell/execute_code/process), minted nothing, and repeated a shape seen in another run, the harness asks YOU instead - one line, at most once per procedure per week. Both are result-text/notice behaviour: no prompt bytes.
agent._comment_nudge_retries: How many times a turn that ends with an intention instead of a tool call - or with no tool call at all - is asked to act again, per run. 0 = ask never, 1 = the old ask-once behaviour; the delivery says 'stopped short' when the budget is spent.
agent._comment_ask_question_ttl: A question a run left unanswered is remembered for the NEXT run and handed to it once; after this many hours it is dropped instead (0 disables the expiry). 24 covers an overnight gap without nagging a box for days.
